Protect your move

Trusting someone with your belongings? Check these first.

Most movers are honest. These five checks, from the federal moving regulator's own advice, help you spot the ones who aren't.

  1. Look up their USDOT number

    Movers that cross state lines must be registered with the FMCSA. You can check any mover's registration for free.

  2. Get the estimate in writing

    Ask whether it's binding or non-binding. On a non-binding interstate estimate, you can't be made to pay more than 110% of it at delivery.

  3. Choose your protection level

    Basic interstate coverage pays only 60 cents per pound per item. Full value protection costs more but covers repair or replacement.

  4. Watch for red flags

    A big cash deposit, a price given without seeing your things, or an unmarked rental truck are all warning signs.

  5. Ask for your rights booklet

    Interstate movers must give you "Your Rights and Responsibilities When You Move" before your move.

Source: FMCSA Protect Your Move

Questions

Frequently asked questions

Still wondering about something? Email hello@liftmyboxes.com and we'll get back to you.

Is the moving cost estimate really free?

Yes. The estimate is free and so is asking for your exact price. Lift My Boxes is paid by the moving companies and networks we connect you with, never by you.

Do I have to give my email or phone number to see a price?

No. You answer a few questions about your move and see your estimate straight away. Contact details are only needed if you decide you want a specialist to confirm your exact price.

How accurate is the estimate?

It is a starting range based on distance, how much you are moving, your date and any extras. Your final price depends on your actual inventory and access at both homes, so a mover confirms it before you book.

Who contacts me if I ask for my exact price?

A moving company or moving network that serves your route and your type of move. You choose whether to go ahead; there is no obligation to book.

Is Lift My Boxes a moving company?

No. We help you estimate the cost of your move and connect you with independent movers when you ask. Before you book any mover, check their USDOT number and get your estimate in writing.

Can you help with pianos, pool tables and hot tubs?

Yes. The calculator has its own options for pianos, pool tables and hot tubs, and requests for those moves go to specialists who handle heavy, awkward items.

Ready to see your number?

It takes about a minute, there's no sign-up, and you're under no obligation to book anything.
